title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
prompt: You are given an array of people, `people`, where `people[i] = [h_i, k_i]` represents a person of height `h_i` with exactly `k_i` other people in front of them who have a height greater than or equal to `h_i`. Reconstruct and return the queue that is represented by these input people, as an array of `[h_i, k_i]` pairs, such that the reconstructed queue satisfies every person's `k_i` constraint.

examples.explanation: This is the unique ordering where each person's k value (number of taller-or-equal people before them) matches.

hints: Trying to place people in their given order and shifting things around gets messy — pick a smarter processing order.
Sort people by height descending, and by k ascending for ties. What does that ordering guarantee about people already placed when you consider the next one?

Insert people one at a time (in that sorted order) into the result list at index k_i. Since every already-placed person is at least as tall, inserting the current person at position k_i automatically gives them exactly k_i taller-or-equal people in front, and later insertions of shorter people won't disturb that count.

solution.approach: Sort people by height in descending order, breaking ties by ascending k. Process people in this order and insert each one into the result list at index k_i. Because taller people are placed first, every person already in the list when a new one is inserted is at least as tall, so inserting at position k_i guarantees exactly k_i taller-or-equal people precede them. Inserting shorter people afterward at their own positions never violates already-satisfied constraints, since those insertions only affect counts among people of equal or lesser height, which don't count toward an earlier person's k value.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) (sorting is O(n log n); each insert into a list is O(n))
